summary: Gérard Colas is an Indologist. He has served as a Directeur de recherche at the National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS, attested 2004, and Senior Fellow in 2009) and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).
Gérard Cotton worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Joseph Mansion and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Liège by 1930.

Gérard Devèze specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Julien Vinson, obtaining a diploma in Tamil from the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales by 1885, and received a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Gérard Fussman specialized in Indology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1961–1965), became a professor at the Collège de France in 1984 succeeding Jean Filliozat, and headed a CNRS unit (attested 1994).

Gérard Huet worked in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics, studying under George Ernst (~1970–1972) and Maurice Nivat (~1972–1976). He served as a professor at Inria (~1974–2017) and supervised numerous doctoral students.

Géza Bethlenfalvy worked in Tibetology and Indology, studying at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under János Harmatta (~1954–1959) and Lajos Ligeti (1963). His career included posts at the University of Delhi (1970) and the University of Vienna (visiting professor, 2007–2008).

Géza Uray was a Tibetologist and linguist who completed his doctorate under Lajos Ligeti in 1942. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (1948–1949, 1979), the Research Centre for Linguistics (~1953–1973), and the University of Pennsylvania (1973–1984).

Gösta Liebert was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Gothenburg and Lund under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He held posts at Lund University (1949–1955), Uppsala University (1951–1953), and served as professor at Gothenburg (1955–1982).

Götz von Selle worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After earning his Dr. phil. at Göttingen (~1914–1920), he held library posts at Göttingen and Berlin, and became honorary professor and library director at Königsberg (1939).
Günter Blamberger held posts at the University of Kassel (~1993–1996) and served as Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne (~1996–2017).

Günter Grönbold specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate under Helmut Hoffmann (~1964–1969). He spent his career at the Bavarian State Library (~1974–2008), where he headed the Oriental Section (~1989–2008).

Günter Lanczkowski worked in religious studies. He studied at Göttingen and Marburg, earning a PhD from Marburg in 1947, and later taught at Heidelberg University (1960–1982), Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1984–1986), and the University of Munich (1986–1988).

Günter Schweiger specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, completing a doctorate under Gert Klingenschmitt. He held posts at Johannes Kepler University Linz (~1966–1968) and served as a full professor at Vienna University of Economics and Business (1974–2009).

Günther Schulemann was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Berlin, Freiburg, and Breslau (Ph.D. ~1910–1913), and later served as Privatdozent (1923) and associate professor of philosophy (1930–1939) at the University of Breslau.

Günther Weibgen was an Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders (~1914–1922). He later worked at the Royal Library of Berlin, succeeding Johannes Nobel in 1928 and becoming Oberbibliothekar in 1944.

Günther-Dietz Sontheimer specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying at Tübingen, ILS Law College, and SOAS under Glasenapp, Bedekar, Kosambi, and Derrett. He spent his academic career at Heidelberg University as an assistant, lecturer, and professor between 1965 and 1979.

H. Craig Melchert is a linguist who studied at Michigan State, DLI, NCS, and Harvard (~1972–1977). He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2007–2015).

H. G. Narahari was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja. By 1944, he was attested as a Research Assistant at the Adyar Library and a Research Fellow at Madras.
H. J. de Graaf worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1919–1926) and under Poerbatjaraka (1927–1930).
H. Kikuchi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 1966, Kikuchi was attested as a research student at the University of Delhi studying under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale.
